extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and industry/PR observers (automotive and marketing audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Coverage of an automotive television commercial that provoked public backlash, focusing on the ad's content, public reaction, and the automaker's response and remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discriminatory or stereotypical content
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercial suggested husbands-to-be give prospective brides the same scrutiny they do a used car — or horse, showing invasive inspection of the bride (opening her mouth, looking at her chest) which many found discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article: mother of the groom opening the bride's mouth to check her teeth and giving a disapproving look at her chest. Anti-pattern: relying on tropes that portray women as passive or controlled by male/family figures. Test creative to ensure it does not reduce people to stereotypes or endorse discriminatory views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider local cultural perceptions and sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: The ad appears to have been intended to play off a Chinese stereotype of fussy parents, but was widely perceived as offensive in China and globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes heavy criticism on Weibo and Tencent (nearly half a million posts). Guidance: evaluate how local stereotypes will be received domestically and internationally; pre-test messaging with local audiences and cultural experts to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency with company values and global brand standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi said the perception created by the ad 'does not correspond to the values of our company in any way.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare new creative against stated corporate values and recent campaigns (e.g., the Super Bowl ad promoting gender equality). Inconsistency between campaigns can damage credibility; companies should maintain brand standards across markets and divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, transparent damage control and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi 'rushed to do damage control', expressed regret, launched an investigation and said it would take steps to ensure the problem isn't repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended actions shown by the article: public statement expressing regret, investigation of how the ad was produced, and commitments to prevent recurrence. Guidance: respond quickly, acknowledge harm, and outline concrete remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain oversight of partner agencies and joint-venture operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The ad was created by an agency for the used-car division of a joint venture Audi operates in China; foreign automakers must partner with local manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When local partners or agencies produce content, the parent company must ensure those partners adhere to global brand and ethical standards. Anti-pattern: assuming partners will automatically align without active review and approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and prioritize brand reputation in key markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi 'can’t afford to alienate Chinese buyers' — China is Audi's most important luxury market and faces intense competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate potential reputation impacts in major markets and prioritize tailored responses where market share or brand dependence is high. Consider competitor landscape and long-term customer relationships when crafting both ads and responses to controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and measure social media and public reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The article highlights extensive social-media criticism (Weibo, Tencent) as the measure of backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social listening to quantify backlash (volume of posts, sentiment) and inform the speed and tone of response. Example metric: 'nearly half a million posts' signaling a major reputational issue requiring escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid objectifying or invasive portrayals of individuals in ads
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes of a mother inspecting the bride (opening her mouth, scrutinizing chest) were perceived as invasive and objectifying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative should avoid framing people as objects for inspection. Anti-pattern examples in the article should be used in internal training to show how visual gags can cross into offensiveness if they target personal attributes or bodily inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate how contrasting campaign messages affect credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese commercial's tone conflicted with a previous Super Bowl spot in which Audi addressed sexism and pledged equal pay — producing a jarring contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a campaign's alignment with prior high-profile messaging; a tone or value reversal can magnify backlash. When a company has publicly taken progressive stances, nearby content perceived as regressive will attract sharper criticism.
